column1: # Colloquial lexicon for the talk texts and mini dialogues (ADR-077), plus the banned list.
# Tab-separated; lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# [allowed] -- spoken words a text may use although the pack may not attest them
# (token rule V1 (c)). One row per form:
#   form, lemma or '-', upos or '-', kind, level, ru gloss, en gloss, reason (>= 10 chars)
#   kind  = particle | interjection | greeting | clipping | contraction | ellipsis | chat
#           (`greeting` also covers thanks and apology formulas; it counts as a marker for
#           the "at least one" rule but not toward the 20% caricature cap)
#   level = A1 | A2 | B1: a text may only use rows up to its band (an A1 text: A1 rows).
# A row with lemma '-' (or a lemma the pack lacks) is exempt from the V2/V3 gates; it
# still counts as a colloquial MARKER (every mini needs >= 1, markers <= 20% of words).
# Single words only (a phrase such as "ne mar" is two rows of the pack's own words).
# Seeded ONLY with items that are real, common and non-vulgar; the evidence is thin
# (research/23-colloquial-register.md) and a native speaker has not read the list.
# [banned] -- vulgar or inappropriate words. A lower-case stem matches every token that
# STARTS with it; a trailing $ means that exact form only (so szar$ does not ban szarvas
# or szarka, and fasz$ does not ban faszekrény). A banned word fails in EVERY
# text, standard ones too, even when the pack attests it.
